subject: Re: Require authentication for checkboxGroupInput selection

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Require authentication for checkboxGroupInput selection
parts:
A couple of thoughts.

From a user experience standpoint, have you considered only showing the checkboxes that the user is allowed to use? And if they are not logged in, have a notice that says "For more options, please sign in"?

Alternately, show all the checkboxes but if they try to use one that they're not allowed to, show the error with a "please sign in" link.

In both cases you'll need to figure out the URL that should be used for the "sign in" link. Probably the easiest way to do this is to turn on required authentication for the app in question, hit it with an unauthenticated browser, and copy the URL that it sends you to (it will have __login__ in the URL path, and a successUrl parameter in the URL query string).

Let me know if it's unclear how to proceed, and we'll give you some more concrete steps or samples.

On Tuesday, June 2, 2015 at 9:53:50 AM UTC-7, Logan Meltabarger wrote:
I am mining various text sources and performing some topic modeling and keyword search functionality via R/Shiny Server Pro. Some of the data sources contain sensitive information so I require AD authentication to view those separate apps for topic modeling through the config files. However, I have ONE app for keyword search that allows the user to select multiple or ALL data sources via checkboxGroupInput. How can I require user authentication when they select some of the checkboxes, but no authentication when they do not select the sensitive sources?

Here is my main panel of ui.R:

 p(strong(h3("Keyword Search"))),
              fluidRow(column(3,
                checkboxGroupInput("dataset",
                                      "Select Feedback Source(s):",
                                      choices = list("Customer Calls"="Call","Employee Feedback"="Employee","Presidential Escalations"="Presidential", "Web Feedback"="Web"),
                                      selected = c("Call","Employee")
                  )), #end checkboxGroupInput
              column(3,offset=6,dateRangeInput("daterange", "Select Date Range:", format = "m/d/yy",
                                 start = Sys.Date()-180, end = Sys.Date(), min = "2010-01-01", max = Sys.Date()                                
               )),#end dateRangeInput
              DT::dataTableOutput('mytable1')
            )#end fluidRow

In the example above, I need two of the four check boxes to require user authentication.

Thanks,
Logan

messages.subject: Re: Require authentication for checkboxGroupInput selection
parts:
> Is there some way to declare a required_group for a checkbox?

No--there's no possible way Shiny Server could know the right thing to do in such a situation.

What you can do is make the app NOT require any authentication from the Shiny Server perspective.

You'd add the following to your shinyServer function:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  user <- session$user
  groups <- session$groups

  # You can now use `user` and `groups` to refer to the signed-in user/groups.
  # These values can be trusted.
  # Any calculations to protected resources MUST check whether the current
  # session is permitted based on the user/groups info, and if not, throw an error.
  # Note that user/groups will be NULL if the session is unauthenticated.

  # These next two lines make "output.isSignedIn" available in conditionalPanels on the client.
  output$isSignedIn <- !is.null(user)
  outputOptions(output, "signedIn", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)


Then somewhere in your ui.R:

conditionalPanel("!output.isSignedIn && (input$checkbox == 1 || input$checkbox == 3)", class = "alert alert-warning",
  HTML("You must be signed in to access this option. Please <a href='login_url'>sign in</a>.")
)

The input$checkbox part of the condition is just an example, I have no idea how you want to determine which options require the user to be logged in.

On Thu, Jun 4, 2015 at 12:21 PM Logan Meltabarger <lrmelt...@gmail.com> wrote:
Let me describe my issue in more detail:

I have 4 different data sources, and each of them have their own app and their own dataset for some sophisticated data topic modeling and trending. Two of them require AD authentication currently because of the data they contain.

Along with those 4 individuals apps, I have one app that acts like a homepage. It has links to the other 4, but its main feature is a DT table that calls a R data set that has all 4 of the apps' text data combined to use for Keyword search. I provide the user checkboxes to filter between the 4 data sources inside the single dataset and a daterange to filter. This is where I want to enable authentication. Inside of this single application based on the selection of checkboxes. I don't want to have them sign-in to the home page or be sent to different apps based on their selection.

"Alternately, show all the checkboxes but if they try to use one that they're not allowed to, show the error with a "please sign in" link." <- this sounds like what I want...I just do not know how to implement the authentication logic since all documentation says required_group or required_user are on a directory (app) level in the config file.

Is there some way to declare a required_group for a checkbox?

Thanks,
Logan
